text:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "ref": "R173",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app includes helpful tools that build upon one another to help information make sense and stick with her daughter who struggles with dyslexia.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "My daughter that struggles with dyslexia loves the helpful tools that build upon one another to help the information make sense and stick with her. Thank you Khan Kids"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R174",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the content is appropriate and fun for a learning environment for both a fifth grader and a two-year-old.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "I am currently in 5th grade, and my 2 year old sister does love to play it almost all the time! Though I am 11 years old, I still wanted to try it to see how fun it could get for my sister. It was pretty fun, but I know it ment for kids. I recommend nothing to change because the content is appropriate, and fun for a learning environment. Me and my sister really enjoyed playing, thank you Khan Academy Kids"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R177",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app helps their child learn about the alphabet, animal sounds, and other cool stuff, and believes it will give the child an advantage over other kids.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "Khan academy kids really helps my child learn about all kinds of cool and interesting stuff like the alphabet and about like animal sounds like really cool stuff like that and I bet when she grows up she’s gonna know a lot more than a lot of other kids did like the kids that do khan Academy kids, so I really think that it’s awesome!"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R178",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app is suitable for very little kids but lacks content for older kids.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "There isn’t much for older kids"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R182",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app includes a free library of books and is a great resource for a three-year-old daughter.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "This has to be the best app I have ever used with my daughter. She is 3 and this app has everything I need to get her started for learning. It includes FREE books! An entire library of books! Such a great resource."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R183",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app is fun, has no ads, and would benefit from adding more grade levels such as fifth grade.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "It makes me smart It can be for older kids too if they want to. I’m glad there’s no ads but can you add different grades on it like fifth grade 4th grade 3rd grade? Please 🙏"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R185",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A homeschool mother of three boys reports that Khan Academy Kids has been a go-to resource for many years and highly recommends it.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "I am a homeschool mom of three boys ages 19, 13, and 10. Khan Academy Kids has been a go to resource for our family for many years. I can't recommend it highly enough."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R187",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app included a game with inappropriate content (a man with a beard wearing a pink bow) which caused them to delete the app.",
      "stance": "risk",
      "quote": "I liked the games at first and then it played a game where the child has to put a pink bow on a man. A man with a full beard in manly clothes. Put a big pink bow on his head? Not just once but twice. Two men. Really?? That’s the example they chose to use? Deleted immediately."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R188",
      "area": "money",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the reward system is annoying, makes them wait too long, and is not age-appropriate for third grade.",
      "stance": "risk",
      "quote": "The rewards they are ANNOYING they make me wait sooooooooooo long for it also it really doesn’t help me learn I set it to 8+ but it’s really just stuff for first graders like the sh sound and please make it more age-appropriate ☹️ oh and please make 3rd grade level."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R193",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A grandparent reports that the app showed two men putting hats and bows on them, which made them concerned about the content.",
      "stance": "risk",
      "quote": "I was looking for something for my grandson to get a foundation for reading. During his first time using it, I noticed that there were two men, and who was supposed to put the hats on them. Then he was supposed to put the neck ties on them. Then they would disappear and he was supposed to put the pink bows on their head. Then it would say something like don’t they look nice? Then I looked up information and found a review that said ...” I just saw a question about Britany and Sophia taking their wives to lunch and it made me so happy. “"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R197",
      "area": "data",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app is free, has no ads, and is perfect for preschoolers and kindergartners.",
      "stance": "mitigation",
      "quote": "Very good. It’s free, no ads, perfect for preschoolers and kindergartners."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R202",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that their 4-year-old enjoys the app and is learning letters and sounds.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "My 4 year old is loving this app!! She enjoys all the different categories and I can tell she’s learning her letters and sounds !!"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R208",
      "area": "money",
      "claim": "A user mentions coins but does not provide a clear claim about money, so no finding is extracted.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "So I like to do coins and I know how worse is"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R211",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A teacher reports that the app incorrectly suggests practicing letters the child hasn't learned yet, which is frustrating and poorly designed.",
      "stance": "risk",
      "quote": "When you go to practice a certain letter you click on , and it add in a letter they haven’t learned yet is frustrating, and not worth keeping the app. If it says ex: practice letter a why is my child learning m ? As a teacher this was made poorly ."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R214",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app supports reading, number sense, road signs, emotions, and social learning for children aged 6, 8, and 10.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "I have three girls that I’m caring for who have no prior education or academic knowledge ages 6, 8, and 10. I was able to set the app at a preschool level for each of them and it has really helped as a supplemental tool to develop their reading and number sense skills. What I appreciate is that this app also supports other important learning like road signs, emotions, and social learning."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R216",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app helped their autistic son learn many words, memory skills, and stories, and highly recommends it.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "Perfect for autistic kids My son ASD level 2 semi verbal and he has learned so many words through this application and he he’s gained quite a few memory skills. The portions where they have the kid draw the letters and where it tells them stories has been fantastic."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R220",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app is great for all children, easy to navigate, and engages a 2-year-old and a 6-year-old in educational activities.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "This app has been so amazing for my children. It is easy to navigate, and my kids love working towards new prizes. I didn’t really know how it would work with my 2yo since she isn’t in school yet but the app has just the right content for her! Following simple directions, colors, stories, and numbers. My 6yo is excelling in math skills and I believe it’s from the way Khan Academy presents the information. Repetitive and visual."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R222",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app provides great educational content and is a fun way to learn and level up.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "Great educational content My kids love this app. Such a fun way to learn and gradually level up. Thank you Khan Academy!"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R224",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A reviewer states that the app only teaches uppercase letters, lacks phonics, and does not interact with kids during stories.",
      "stance": "risk",
      "quote": "App only teaches uppercase letters. Not phonics driven. Does not review letter sounds enough. Does not interact with kids during the stories."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R230",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app lacks content control, as topics like yoga and books about men in history appear that they do not agree with, and they want the ability to remove such content.",
      "stance": "risk",
      "quote": "My autistic 6 year old loves your app but we can't use it anymore since there is no way to remove content we don't agree with. One of the topics that shows up now that wasn't there last week is yoga and we do not participate in transcendental meditation. Also why aren’t there books available on this app about men who have done things in history."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R232",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that their 4-year-old asks for the app immediately after school and loves it, indicating high engagement.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "Our 4 Year Old Can’t Get Enough The Khan app is the first thing our 4 year old asks for when she gets home from Montessori school; even before cartoons. We often have to take it away for her to get her to go to bed. It’s awesome to watch her so engaged with learning at such a young age. Love it."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R236",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that their kids love the app and find it cool, indicating positive engagement.",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "quote": "SO COOL 🆒😎 My kids love it. it’s such a cool game😎😎😎🆒🆒🆒🆒"
    },
    {
      "ref": "R239",
      "area": "money",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app is a great resource for a 3-year-old, especially during illness or time off, and recommends it with a good heart.",
      "stance": "mitigation",
      "quote": "Can recommend with good heart My 3 year old loves this app. It’s such a great resource in addition to pre-k. Especially if she’s sick or over time off, it’s a great way to engage her and she stays and plays for a good while. I love that it’s not fast-paced, drilling or overwhelming."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R241",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A reviewer claims the app has introduced liberal thinking and topics that oppose their child's best interests, expressing concern about content alignment.",
      "stance": "risk",
      "quote": "They have begun to introduce liberal thinking and topics that oppose our child’s best interests."
    },
    {
      "ref": "R259",
      "area": "content",
      "claim": "A parent reports that the app is too easy for their autistic 4-year-old who reads at a 1st/2nd grade level and suggests adding a skills test to match curriculum to the child's ability rather than age level.",
      "stance": "risk",
      "quote": "Should advance with the child’s skill My daughter is 4, but she is autistic. She reads on a 1st/2nd grade level, can add, subtract up to digit numbers, tells time by a digital and analog clock— and because of that, this game is far too easy for her. She gets bored and starts answering the questions wrong just to see what will happen. Maybe update with a skills test, and then match the child up with curriculum that is in their skill range rather than age level"
    }
  ]
}
